relevance_note: Case report of a Blau syndrome patient with a NOD2 variant ('she had a de-novo heterozygous mutation in the NOD2 gene'), plus a supplementary table of 8 Blau syndrome children from the same centre and a literature table of published Blau-vasculitis cases.
method_note: Read the whole paper; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON, took table cells and row-prefix spans directly from the Markdown lines, and asserted every span verbatim; transcribed cells were checked against the tables by eye. Case patient labelled 'patient' (rule 5). She is evidently also Table S row 7 (Female, diagnosed 2019, onset 0.83, first visit 7.67 = '7 years and 8 months', diagnosis 17.83, M513T, V/HBP/RI marked) and Table 1 row 11 ('2022,Our medical center'); the paper does not say so explicitly, but the details match, so she is one row ('patient'), not a separate 'Table S #7'. Her Table S row lists F, V, HBP and RI, consistent with the text. Table S (supplement, centre cohort of 8): bare numbers in column 'No' give labels 'Table S #n'. '*' is defined as present; blank cells are not reported (no definition of blank as absent). Ages are in years per header 'Age(year)'; columns used: Onset, Diagnosis (the 'First visit' age is not recorded); ISO durations kept as decimal years (e.g. P0.33Y). Patient #3 has Mutation 'NA': no variant row. Table S does not print the gene name, so gene_symbol_as_stated is 'not reported' for Table S variants. 'M513A' (#6) recorded exactly as printed. RI (renal involvement), LI (liver involvement), CI (cardiac involvement) are too unspecific for the checklist items (granulomatous nephritis/renal failure, hepatomegaly/hepatic granulomas, pericarditis) and are left not reported there; they are recorded as phenotypic_features. Table 1 (literature review): rows without a patient label column, labelled 'Table 1 row k' (k = data rows from top, excluding the second header line); source cell copied to source_reference_in_review. Rows 1 (Rotenstein [8], '2/F', two patients) and 10 (Li [17], '8/NA', eight patients) describe groups with no fact attributable to one person, so they get no rows. Row 11 is the case patient. '^a' is defined as present; blank and NA cells are not reported. Table 1 variants (R334W, G464W, D382E) take gene NOD2 from the sentence naming these three mutations 'in the NOD2 gene'. Checklist vasculitis: 'stated for this individual' where the cell names arteritis/aortitis/vasculitis (rows 3,5,7,8,9; row 5 cell reads only 'large-vessel'); for rows 2 (renal/mesenteric artery stenosis), 4 (abdominal aortic aneurysm) and 6 (sinus of Valsalva aneurysm) it is inferred from the table title that all listed cases had Blau syndrome and vasculitis. Time-dependent findings for the case patient (not treated as contradictions): CRP and ESR significantly increased in 2009, within normal ranges in October 2019, ESR increased (25 mm/h) in December 2022; rash at 10 months but 'no rashes' in December 2022; no ocular findings at the 2009 referral but uveitis at 7 and panuveitis in 2019. Checklist set to observed for these; both feature rows emitted with timing in severity_or_detail. Normal whole examinations (echocardiography/ECG, aorta/cerebrovascular imaging, 'No other remarkable findings' on physical examination) exclude nothing more specific (D-27); impaired renal function / raised creatinine not mapped to 'renal failure'. n_patients_reported left null: the authors give no single count of NOD2-variant patients described. cohort_size_as_stated = 8 (centre cohort in Table S). No contradictions found inside the paper.

Finally, she temporarily accepted a low dose of oral prednisolone, MTX, metoprolol and plendil.
